title: Master Data II — Product, Info Records, Source Lists
intro: The material (product) master describes what you buy and stock. Purchasing info records and source lists describe who you buy it from and on what terms.
objectives: Explain material types, views and organisational levels of the material master
Identify the key purchasing, MRP and accounting fields
Create and use purchasing info records
Use source lists and explain the source determination sequence

lessons.title: Material master structure
lessons.body:
The material master (called product master in Fiori) is the central record for everything a company buys, makes, stores or sells. Transactions: MM01 create, MM02 change, MM03 display. Fiori: Manage Product Master Data.

Material type

Chosen at creation; controls which views are allowed, numbering, and whether quantity and value are tracked.

TypeMeaning
ROHRaw material
HALBSemi-finished product
FERTFinished product
HAWATrading goods (bought and resold)
HIBEOperating supplies
ERSASpare parts
VERPPackaging
NLAGNon-stock material
DIENService

Views and organisational levels

Data is split into views, each held at an organisational level:

ViewLevel
Basic dataClient
Purchasing, MRP, Plant dataPlant
Storage location dataStorage location
Accounting, CostingValuation area (plant)
SalesSales org / distribution channel

So the same material can have different MRP settings in Fréjus and Nice, but always the same description and base unit.

In S/4HANA the material number can be up to 40 characters (18 in ECC).
lessons.narration: The material master, called the product master in Fiori, is the central record for everything a company buys, makes, stores or sells. You create it with M M zero one, change it with M M zero two, and display it with M M zero three. When you create a material, you choose a material type, and that choice controls which data views are allowed, how the number is assigned, and whether stock quantity and value are tracked. The common types are R O H for raw materials, H A L B for semi-finished products, F E R T for finished products, H A W A for trading goods that you buy and resell, H I B E for operating supplies, E R S A for spare parts, V E R P for packaging, N L A G for non-stock materials, and D I E N for services. The data itself is split into views, and each view lives at an organisational level. Basic data, such as the description and base unit of measure, is held at client level, so it's the same everywhere. Purchasing, M R P and plant data are held per plant. Storage location data is per storage location. Accounting and costing data are per valuation area, which is normally the plant. And sales data is per sales organisation and distribution channel. That means one material can have different planning settings in two plants, but always the same description. Finally, in S/4HANA, material numbers can be up to forty characters long.
keyTerms: Controls views, numbering and quantity/value update, e.g. ROH, FERT, HAWA
Section of the material master, e.g. Purchasing, MRP 1, Accounting 1
Client-level data: description, base unit, material group
Non-stock material: bought for consumption, no inventory

lessons.title: Key fields for purchasing, planning and accounting
lessons.body:
Basic data

  • Base unit of measure: the unit stock is managed in (e.g. PC, KG)
  • Material group: groups similar materials for purchasing and reporting

Purchasing view (plant)

  • Order unit: unit used on POs if different from base unit (e.g. order in boxes, stock in pieces), with conversion factors
  • Purchasing group: responsible buyer
  • Under/overdelivery tolerance and unlimited overdelivery
  • Source list indicator: a source list is required for this material in this plant
  • GR processing time: days between receipt and availability

MRP views (plant)

  • MRP type and lot size (Module 9)
  • Planned delivery time
  • Procurement type: E in-house, F external, X both

Accounting 1 view (valuation area)

  • Valuation class: links the material to G/L accounts (Module 7)
  • Price control: S standard price or V moving average price
  • Standard price / moving average price

Price control and valuation class decide what happens in accounting at every goods receipt and invoice. Trainers who understand these two fields can explain almost any posting.
lessons.narration: Let's look at the fields that matter most. In basic data, the base unit of measure is the unit stock is managed in, such as pieces or kilograms, and the material group groups similar materials for purchasing and reporting. In the purchasing view, which is held per plant, you'll find the order unit, used when you order in a different unit, for example ordering boxes but stocking pieces. There's the purchasing group, the responsible buyer. There are under-delivery and over-delivery tolerances. There's the source list indicator, which forces a source list for this material in this plant. And there's the goods receipt processing time, the number of days between receipt and availability. In the M R P views, you set the M R P type, the lot size, the planned delivery time, and the procurement type: E for in-house production, F for external procurement, or X for both. In the accounting one view, two fields are critical. The valuation class links the material to general ledger accounts. And price control decides how stock is valued: S for standard price, which stays fixed, or V for moving average price, which changes with each receipt. If you understand these two fields, you can explain almost every accounting posting in MM.
keyTerms: Purchasing unit different from base unit, with conversion
E in-house, F external, X both
Links the material to G/L accounts
Standard price: fixed; differences go to a price difference account
Moving average price: recalculated at receipts

lessons.title: Purchasing info records
lessons.body:
A purchasing info record stores the relationship between one material and one supplier: price, delivery time, tolerances. When a buyer creates a PO, the price is proposed from it.

Transactions: ME11 create, ME12 change, ME13 display. Fiori: Manage Purchasing Info Records.

Data levels

  • General data: supplier material number, reminders, origin
  • Purchasing organisation (and plant) data: planned delivery time, purchasing group, standard quantity, tolerances, net price and conditions (prices, discounts, surcharges with validity periods)

Info record categories

  • Standard: normal purchasing
  • Subcontracting: price for the subcontractor's work
  • Consignment: price for consignment stock withdrawals
  • Pipeline: e.g. utilities, oil, gas

How they get created

  • Manually with ME11
  • Automatically from a PO or quotation when the Info Update indicator is set on the item
  • Without a material number, for a material group (e.g. office supplies)

The info record also shows the last PO number and price history: a great live demo of “the system remembers”.
lessons.narration: A purchasing info record stores the relationship between one material and one supplier. It holds the price, the delivery time and the tolerances, and when a buyer creates a purchase order, the price is proposed from it. You create one with M E one one, change it with M E one two, and display it with M E one three. An info record has two levels. General data includes the supplier's own material number and reminder settings. Purchasing organisation data, optionally per plant, holds the planned delivery time, purchasing group, tolerances, and most importantly the conditions: the prices, discounts and surcharges, each with a validity period. There are four categories of info record: standard, for normal purchasing; subcontracting, for the price of a subcontractor's work; consignment, for the price of consignment stock; and pipeline, for things like utilities. Info records can be created manually, or automatically from a purchase order or quotation when the info update indicator is set on the item. They can even be created without a material number, for a material group such as office supplies. A nice classroom demo: open an info record and show the last purchase order number and price history. It shows learners that the system remembers.
keyTerms: Material–supplier relationship with price and terms
Prices, discounts and surcharges with validity periods
PO item flag that creates/updates the info record

lessons.title: Source lists and source determination
lessons.body:
A source list defines the allowed sources for a material in a plant over a period of time. Transaction: ME01 (maintain). Fiori: Manage Source Lists.

Each source list line contains

  • Validity dates
  • Supplier and purchasing organisation (or an outline agreement)
  • Fixed indicator: preferred source for the period
  • Blocked indicator: source not allowed
  • MRP indicator: whether MRP may assign this source automatically

When is a source list required?

  • If set in the material master purchasing view, or
  • If required for all materials in a plant (configuration)

Then a PO can only be created with a supplier in the source list.

Source determination sequence

When the system looks for a supplier (e.g. for a requisition), it checks in this order:

  1. Quota arrangement (split between suppliers by percentage, MEQ1)
  2. Source list
  3. Outline agreements (contracts, scheduling agreements)
  4. Info records

Source lists are a compliance tool: they stop buyers ordering from unapproved suppliers.
lessons.narration: A source list defines which sources are allowed for a material in a plant, over a period of time. You maintain it with M E zero one. Each line has validity dates, a supplier and purchasing organisation or an outline agreement, and three important indicators. Fixed marks the preferred source for that period. Blocked means the source isn't allowed. And the M R P indicator decides whether planning can assign this source automatically. A source list becomes mandatory either through the indicator in the material's purchasing view, or through a plant-wide setting in configuration. Once it's required, a purchase order can only be created with a supplier that's in the list. When the system looks for a supplier automatically, for example for a requisition, it follows a set sequence. First, quota arrangements, which split requirements between suppliers by percentage. Then the source list. Then outline agreements, meaning contracts and scheduling agreements. And finally info records. For trainers, it's worth framing source lists as a compliance tool: they stop buyers ordering from suppliers that haven't been approved.
keyTerms: Allowed sources per material and plant with validity periods
Splits requirements between sources by percentage (MEQ1)
Quota → source list → outline agreement → info record

quiz.q: Which material type is used for goods bought and resold without processing?
At which level is the material description held?
quiz.explain: Basic data, including the description, is client level.

quiz.q: A material with price control V is valued at…
quiz.explain: V = moving average price, recalculated at goods receipts and invoices.

quiz.q: What does a purchasing info record contain?
quiz.explain: Info records hold prices, conditions and delivery terms for a material–supplier pair.

quiz.q: How can an info record be created automatically?
options: From a PO item with the Info Update indicator
quiz.explain: The Info Update indicator on PO or quotation items updates or creates the info record.

quiz.q: Which comes first in source determination?
quiz.explain: Quota arrangement → source list → outline agreement → info record.

quiz.q: A source list entry with the 'blocked' indicator means…
options: The supplier may not be used in that period
The PO is blocked for payment
quiz.explain: Blocked sources cannot be used for the material/plant in that period.

quiz.q: Which field links a material to inventory G/L accounts?
quiz.explain: The valuation class drives automatic account determination.
E = in-house, F = external, X = both.
